content:
- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 7-day average.
- Underestimate late-period price surges (last 5–7 days of history) — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% if recent history shows accelerating upward trend.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >8% from prior day) — cap forecast at +5% above prior day’s close or use 3-day moving average as ceiling.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged response: if true outcome is >10% above forecast, model often underreacts — adjust next forecast by +1.5% of the gap to correct lag.
- Avoid overfitting to recent volatility — if last 3 days show high variance, reduce forecast sensitivity to short-term noise by smoothing with 5-day EWMA.
